transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I suppose… what finally made me say something is that after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up. And then I come back down and sort of act like I was just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed, as if nothing’s happened.

It feels awful to say out loud, honestly. I’ve been trying to keep it very contained, very hidden, almost like if I do it quietly and no one notices then it doesn’t count somehow. But it does, and I know it’s not right. That’s really why I’m here.
How often have you been making yourself vomit after eating, and does it usually follow a specific pattern, like after eating large amounts of food in a short period?

It’s… it’s usually after I feel I’ve eaten too much. Not just a normal meal, or at least I don’t think of it that way in the moment — it’s when I feel I’ve gone past some line, and then I get this panic and I go upstairs.

I don’t usually make a fuss or draw attention to it. I’ll sort of wait until it seems natural to leave the room, and then I make myself sick. Afterwards I come back down and act as though I’ve just been tidying the kitchen, or getting ready for bed, or doing something ordinary. I’m very aware of how deliberate that sounds, and I hate saying it, but that is the pattern, really. It’s hidden around the evening routine, if that makes sense.

As for how often… I find that harder to say neatly, because I’ve been trying not to count it, almost. But it has been happening enough that I couldn’t keep pretending it was just a one-off or something I had under control.
Besides making yourself vomit, have you also been doing anything else like exercising a lot, skipping meals, or using laxatives or diuretics to try to control your weight or shape?

Yes… not so much tablets or anything like that, but I do other things, yes. The next day especially, if I feel I’ve really overdone it the night before, I’ll sort of make these rules for myself. I’ll tell myself I don’t need breakfast, and then by lunchtime I’ll still be saying, “No, just wait, you had enough yesterday,” as if that somehow balances it out.

And with walking as well — I go with a walking group, which on the face of it sounds perfectly healthy and ordinary, and I suppose it can be. But sometimes I’ll push myself to do extra laps, or go further than I really feel like going, not because I’m full of energy or enjoying it particularly, but because I’m trying to undo what I ate. It’s that sort of bargain in my head: if I skip those meals, or if I walk enough, maybe I can cancel it out.

I know that probably sounds very calculated, but at the time it feels almost like I have to do it, like I won’t be able to settle otherwise.
When you eat, do you ever feel like you can't control how much you're eating or feel like you can't stop eating, even if you wanted to?

Yes. That’s probably the part that frightens me most, actually, because it doesn’t feel like ordinary overeating, like deciding to have another biscuit and then regretting it. It’s more like… once I start, something changes. Like a switch flips.

I’ll be aware I’m doing it, but not in a way that seems to help. Part of me will be thinking, “Linda, stop now. You’ve had enough. Put it away.” And at the same time my hands are still reaching for more, or I’m still going back to the cupboard or the fridge. It’s horrible because I’m not unconscious or anything — I know what I’m doing — but it feels as though the sensible part of me has been pushed to the side and I’m sort of watching myself carry on.

And then the more I eat, the more panicky I get, but that panic doesn’t make me stop. If anything, it all becomes very rushed and automatic, like I’ve already ruined it so I might as well keep going. I’m embarrassed saying that, because it sounds so irrational, but in those moments it really does feel like I can’t stop even though I desperately want to.
